observations: A figure stands slightly left of center, one pale forearm raised to cross in front of a large dark mass that fills the upper half of the image, covering where a head would be.
Red scribbled lines run through and around the dark mass over deeper black and brown tones; the figure wears a yellow-green top and blue lower garment.
The background is saturated yellow-orange, built from overlapping broad vertical strokes pressing in from both sides, with a darker shadow zone directly behind the figure.
reading: The raised arm blocks the face entirely, so the figure reads as closed-off rather than confrontational. Yellow-orange presses in from every edge, bright and insistent, while the dark mass above absorbs that light. The red scribble lines feel agitated against the stillness of the pale arm. That tension—warmth surrounding withdrawal—gives the image its pull.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between nnotb #136 and nnotb #138 in both title order and recorded creation order. Where #136 fills its surface with dense, high-contrast line work and many colors, #137 reduces to three dominant zones: yellow surround, dark mass, pale limb.

connections.reason: nnotb #138 shares a single figure centered against a dark background with warm color pressing in from the sides, though its scribbled marks are black rather than red and the figure faces outward rather than turning away.

tags: red scribble lines on dark mass
lookingQuestion: Where exactly does the pale arm meet the dark mass above it, and what happens to the red lines at that boundary?
ambiguities: The dark form above the figure's shoulders is ambiguous—it reads as hair or a large organic mass but cannot be confirmed from the image alone.
nnotb #136 shares title-neighbor and recorded-creation-neighbor status but its visual language is so different that no strong formal connection was found; it was not selected as a connection.
